findings.title: Description references secrets/credentias
findings.detail: Description of "ship_check" references sensitive artifacts (password, secret, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_availability" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List open slots for a free 30-minute intro call with Matt Turley (Continuum), read live from his Cal.com calendar. Use it when the user wants to talk to Matt, g…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: ship_check, request_human_review, book_call, request_estimate · Private data: ship_check, send_message · Public sink: request_human_review, list_services, book_call, send_message, request_estimate · Destructive: ship_check, swarm_run_cost_estimate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: ship_check, request_human_review, book_call, request_estimate · Private data: ship_check, send_message · Public sink: request_human_review, list_services, book_call, send_message, request_estimate · Destructive: ship_check, swarm_run_cost_estimate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
